# connection:jst-eh-3pin

**JST EH 3-circuit wire-to-board joint, 2.5 mm pitch — the DYNAMIXEL TTL socket, and every cable end on the Microduck's servo bus**

## What it joins

- **a** — an EH cable housing (interface name `mate`, role `eh_housing`) — part:jst-ehr-03, i.e. either end of part:cable-dxl-x3p, carrying three part:jst-seh-001t-p0.6 crimps
- **b** — an EH top-entry Type A board header (interface name `mate`, role `eh_header`) — part:jst-b3b-eh-a, or the socket cut into part:xl330-m288-t's own case (interfaces `socket_pos_y` / `socket_neg_y`)

## Verdict: PASS

THE GEOMETRY OF THE PAIR IS PASS AND IT IS DERIVED, NOT RECALLED: the 1.6000 mm seat falls out of 8.1000 - 6.5000 and is independently printed as '(1.6)' on the header's own side view; the contact rows coincide at x = -2.5000 / 0.0000 / +2.5000 on both sides; the housing's 3.8000 mm thickness equals the header's 3.8000 mm, so the pair is the 3.8 x 8.1 envelope eEH.pdf p.1 states in words. THE ELECTRICAL SIDE OF THIS JOINT IS WHERE THE MICRODUCK HAS A PROBLEM, and it is recorded here rather than softened — see `findings`.

## What it adds to the BOM

`part:jst-ehr-03`, `part:jst-seh-001t-p0.6`, `part:jst-b3b-eh-a`

A made joint is three folders, not one: the housing (1 per end), the crimp (3 per end — the contacts are 'Sold Separately' on eEH.pdf p.2), and the header on the board side. mate() returns them as a BOM with those quantities. When side b is a servo the header is INSIDE the bought servo and is NOT added — part:xl330-m288-t already carries it, and adding it again would double-count; mate() drops it by name when b's interface belongs to part:xl330-m288-t.

## The joint

- holds by **contact friction plus the housing's 0.6 mm lock rib**, removable: True, transmits
